sources.title: 16 CFR Part 23 — Guides for the Jewelry, Precious Metals, and Pewter Industries (eCFR, current)
sources.publisher: U.S. Government (eCFR / Office of the Federal Register)
sources.used_for: Legal basis for gold quality marks, the 10-karat minimum for describing an item as gold, and §23.10 quality-mark guidance.
sources.verification: Official index entry retrieved in this session; §23.10 and §23.4 excerpts confirmed through the Federal Register final rule (SRC-FR-2018). Full sections were not read line-by-line — see flag F-11.

sources.title: Federal Register 83 FR 40659 — Guides for the Jewelry, Precious Metals, and Pewter Industries (final revisions, 2018-08-16)
sources.used_for: Verbatim basis for: quality-mark definition (§23.10); Note 2 to §23.10 — the National Stamping Act requires the trademark or name of the manufacturer/dealer to be applied next to a quality mark; §23.4 — gold descriptions below 10 karat are improper.
sources.quoted: “The National Stamping Act provides that any person, firm, corporation, or association, being a manufacturer or dealer ... who applies or causes to be applied a quality mark ... shall apply to the article the trademark or name of such person.” (Note 2 to § 23.10)
sources.verification: Official page retrieved in this session; excerpt above read from the retrieved document.
